newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand forces mergers of ailing finance firms.
newsitem.headline: Thailand forces mergers of ailing finance firms.

text.p: Thailand's top finance authorities on Friday took a decisive step to avert disaster in the troubled finance sector by forcing 16 ailing companies to be absorbed by healthy ones.

The companies were asked to suspend operations immediately for 30 days and given two weeks to come up with plans to shape up or have their business licences revoked and be absorbed by healthier firms under a purchase and assumption arrangement.
The list of suspended firms included former top Thai finance firm Finance One Plc and other well-known ones such as General Finance and Securities Plc and CMIC Finance and Securities.
Others suspended were:
Dynamic Eastern Finance Thailand Plc, Prime Finance and Securities, ITF Finance and Securities Plc and Thai Financial Trust Plc.

CL Sahaviriya Finance and Securities, United Finance Corp Plc. GCN Finance Plc, Sub Thamrong Finance Co Ltd, Thai Fuji Finance and Securities, Thana One Finance and Securities Co Ltd, Country Finance Co Ltd, Srinakorn Finance and Securities Co Ltd and Royal International Finance and Securities Co Ltd.

Thai stocks, which rallied 2.37 percent early in the day on foreign buying, dropped back after the merger news hit the market. The SET index was 0.52 points or 0.10 percent lower to 519.50 by the lunchbreak.

"The package is a part of measures to strengthen the sector. I am confident that the measures that we launched and will implement are in the right direction," Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond told a news conference.
"I believe it will restore foreign investor confidence in Thailand," he added.

A central bank source said the 16 firms were singled out for the forced action because either their assets were lower than one third of their capital or their borrowings from the central bank's funds had topped 40 percent of outstanding deposits.

Thailand's beleagured finance sector has been hard hit since the economic bubble burst last year after a decade of booming business. The Thai economy is now in a severe downturn and authorities are struggling to put it on an even keel.
The finance sector faces severe liquidity problems amid high interest rates and its asset quality is deteriorating fast due to overexposure to the depressed property sector.
Private sector estimates put the extent of finance company non-performing loans now at 31.5 percent of all outstanding loans. But Rerngchai declined to comment on this.

In a move to avert the financial meltdown, the government earlier this week issued decrees to allow more than 25 percent foreign equity participation in financial institutions. The decrees also sought to smoothe out processes for mergers and acquisitions in the finance sector.
Five major finance firms were chosen by the authorities to lead the upcoming mergers in the sector.
They were Dhana Siam Finance and Securities Plc, National Finance and Securities Plc, Nava Finance and Securities, Krungthai Thanakit Plc and Phatra Thanakit Finance Securities Plc.

After mergers take place with the leading firms, the new entities may apply for new banking licences. But the central bank said it will only give between two and five new licences to qualified parties with assets of 150 billion baht ($6 billion).
Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said the depositors of the ailing 16 finance firms would be fully protected and their debtors would be allowed to carry on their business.
"I would like to assure depositors that they will be safe. Under the purchase and assumption scheme, bigger and healthier firms will absorb only good assets from these troubled companies," he said.
"And that includes depositors' money," he added.
